source_text: Nam cum utrumque ex more dicatur, aliquando quod diabolum quis imitatus, invideat; aliquando quod hominem aemulatus, aut invidia, aut flagitiosorum sordibus oblinatur; hoc quoque imitationis nomen utrique possit convenire personae, id est, et cum de homine, et cum de diabolo dicitur; tu perridicule ineptire voluisti, per imitationis intellectum Adam non potuisse monstrari.
pass_a_gloss: For since both are said from custom, sometimes that someone, having imitated the devil, envies; sometimes that, having rivaled a human being, he is smeared either with envy or with the filths of the shameful; this name also of imitation can fit either person, that is, both when it is said of a human being and when of the devil; you wanted to play the fool most ridiculously, that through an understanding of imitation Adam could not have been shown.

lemmas.lexica: LS imitatio; Blaise moral copying vs generation of sin

pass_b_english: Both expressions are customary. Sometimes a person envies because he has imitated the devil; sometimes, by copying a human being, he is stained with envy or the filth of shameful conduct. The word ‘imitation’ can therefore apply to either person, whether one is speaking of a human being or of the devil. Your insistence that Adam could not have been indicated in connection with imitation is ridiculously foolish.

choices.why: Julian's Rom 5:12 reading: sin passes by copying Adam's example, not by generation/seed.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
